description.summary: Recursive Chunking splits source content through ordered structural or separator rules before falling back to smaller boundaries.
description.description: Recursive Chunking is a RAG technique that attempts to split content at higher-level boundaries such as sections or paragraphs, then falls back to smaller separators when chunks exceed the configured size.
description.problemStatement: Naive fixed-size splitting can cut through paragraphs, sections, or other meaningful document structure that may be useful for retrieval.
description.coreIdea: Apply an ordered hierarchy of separators or structural boundaries so chunks stay within size limits while preserving source structure when possible.

inputRequirements.name: Structured or semi-structured source content
inputRequirements.description: Documents or text content with separators, paragraphs, sections, or other boundaries that can guide splitting.

outputArtifacts.name: Structure-aware chunks
outputArtifacts.description: Chunk artifacts produced by applying ordered splitting rules to source content.

implementationConsiderations: Tune separator order and maximum chunk size for the document formats in the corpus.
Inspect source formatting because inconsistent separators can produce uneven or less coherent chunks.
evaluationGuidance: Compare chunk coherence and retrieval results against a fixed-size baseline on representative documents.
